newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends firmer on central bank defence.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends firmer on central bank defence.

text.p: A persistent defence by the central bank pushed the Taiwan dollar to a slightly firmer close against its U.S. counterpart on Friday despite heavy greenback buying, dealers said.

The local unit ended at T$28.724 against Thursday's T$28.725 close following strong defence by the central bank to prevent the Taiwan dollar from falling below T$28.727 level over the past few sessions.
Turnover through dealers was very heavy at US$491.5 million, up from Thursday's US$237 million.
"Nobody knows why the central bank chose to defend the Taiwan dollar at T$28.727, but it's apparant the central bank wants to maintain stability," said one dealer at a foreign bank.
Dealers said the Taiwan dollar faced strong depreciation pressure due to heavy buying from local importers and offshore speculators.
"The U.S. dollar buying is active both at home and abroad and the central bank seems to be the sole seller in the market," said another dealer.
"Currency jitters in many southeast Asian nations trigger offshore greenback buying," the second dealer said.
The Malaysian ringgit hit an all-time low on Friday.
"The central bank is sending a strong message -- the Taiwan dollar is not like other southeastern Asian currencies," the dealer said.
The central bank has repeatedly said it would intervene to defend the local currency if "abnormal" factors -- including offshore speculation -- occur.
Dealers saw a stable range for Saturday.
